newsitem.title: DUBAI: U.S. carrier leaves Gulf, still in Fifth Fleet area.
newsitem.headline: U.S. carrier leaves Gulf, still in Fifth Fleet area.

text.p: The United States withdrew its aircraft carrier Carl Vinson from the Gulf on Wednesday, but the ship was still in the U.S. Fifth Fleet's area of operations, U.S. officials in the Middle East said.
"The Carl Vinson left the Gulf waters today and went through the Strait of Hormuz. It is currently in the Gulf of Oman and is still part of Fifth Fleet," an official told Reuters.
The officials said the carrier was set to leave Fifth Fleet area -- which extends from the Red Sea and Horn of Africa in the west to Pakistan in the east -- next week and head back home.
Its departure leaves only one U.S. carrier, the Enterprise, in the waterway near Iraq and officials said that ship was still carrying out its mission to watch over southern Iraq.
U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry said last week Iraq was "backing off" from a recent confrontation with Washington.

The Enterprise was moved to the Gulf from the Adriatic two weeks ago to join the Vinson in a U.S. military buildup in the region after Iraqi President Saddam Hussein's forces supported one Kurdish militia group against another in northern Iraq.

Iraq at first vowed to keep shooting missiles at U.S. and allied aircraft, but later promised to suspend such attacks, which followed a strike by U.S. air- and sea-launched cruise missiles against air defence targets in southern Iraq.
